summary: This Dockerfile builds a Ubuntu container with Zsh and Git pre-installed, then configures a shell function that displays the three most recently modified Git branches whenever you change directories or run git status. It also creates a demo Git repository with three branches at different ages to showcase the feature in action.

explanations.3: This tells the installer to skip interactive prompts during setup, so the build won't hang waiting for user input.
explanations.6: The --no-install-recommends flag skips optional packages, keeping the image smaller and faster to build.
explanations.9: After installing packages, we delete the cached package lists to reduce the final image size.
explanations.12: The printf command with '%s\n' takes multiple string arguments and prints each one on a new line, effectively building a multi-line shell script.
explanations.31: The $'...' syntax in Bash/Zsh allows escape sequences like \e for color codes; the \e[1;36m makes cyan bold text.
explanations.53: The >> appends all those printf lines to the .zshrc file (the shell config file), rather than overwriting it.
explanations.63: We're setting the commit date to 100 days ago so the main branch appears old compared to the other branches.
explanations.68: The -b flag creates and switches to a new branch in one command.
explanations.88: The -i flag runs Zsh interactively (with a prompt) and -l runs it as a login shell (sources config files like .zshrc).
